عَضِدٌ Having a complaint of his عَضُد [or upper arm]. (O, K.) ―
-b2- A camel having the disease termed عَضَدٌ. (TA.) ―
-b3- One that has drawn near, or approached, to the عَضُدَانِ [i. e. the two sides] (O, TA) of the watering-trough, or tank. (O, K.) ―
-b4- A male [wild] ass that has drawn together the she-asses (الأُتُنَ) from their several quarters (مِنْ جَوَانِبِهَا); as also ↓ عَاضِدٌ : (O, K:) the former occurs in a verse of El-Akhtal, describing a sportsman shooting at [wild] asses. (O.) ―
-b5- يَدٌ عَضِدَةٌ An arm of which the عَضُد [or portion between the elbow and the shoulder-blade] is short. (ISk, S, O, K.) And عَضُدٌ عَضِدَةٌ A short upper arm. (TA.) ＝
-A2- See also عَضُدٌ, first sentence. ―
-b2- And see عَضَادٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
